theater.name: Houthis / Red Sea
theater.title: Houthis / Red Sea
theater.sub: The options the US has toward the Houthis in Yemen and the Red Sea, and what followed the last times the US did something like each one.
theater.actor: the Houthis or another Iran-backed group
theater.proxy_note: Iran arms the Houthis, so seizures of Iranian arms bound for them are option E. A reply by another Iran-backed group would be labelled "proxy"; none is logged here.
theater.hold_note: Hold cases are weeks, from Nov 20, 2023 on, with no logged US sanctions, naval, strike or posture move. Weeks inside the long stretches of fighting (Jan 12, 2024 - Jan 19, 2025 and Mar 15 - May 6, 2025) are left out, because US activity there was continuous. Most hold weeks fall in 2025-2026 and most have no logged event at all. The log for 2025-2026 records only major events, so a week where "nothing happened" may only be a week where nothing was logged. Read option A as a rough sketch, and do not compare it number-for-number with options that rest on a few well-reported cases.
theater.not_measured: Oil and freight prices, ship insurance costs, harm to ordinary Yemenis and strain with Saudi Arabia are not measured.
theater.under_logged: Some stretches are logged more thinly than others (2025-2026 far less than 2024), so "none logged" is not proof nothing happened.

political.other: Share of past cases NOT followed within 14 days by any logged diplomatic event (talks, a ceasefire, a UN resolution, or a public statement or threat by either side).
political.hold: Share of hold weeks NOT followed within 14 days by any logged diplomatic event (talks, a ceasefire, a UN resolution, or a public statement or threat by either side).
political.rule: Counts when no diplomatic event of any kind was logged in the 14 days after, by anyone. Public statements and threats count as diplomatic events here (for example Trump's Jul 21 and Jul 23, 2026 warnings), so a threat alone makes the case "not a risk" on this corner.

hostile.title: Two missiles, believed to be Chinese-made C-802s, are fired at the destroyer USS Mason near Bab el-Mandeb; the Mason fires defensive missiles (USNI dates this Oct 9; the Pentagon calls Oct 12 the 'second time in four days')
Second missile attack on the Mason in four days; the Pentagon says at least one missile came from Houthi-controlled territory near Al Hudaydah and the crew used countermeasures

USS Nitze fires Tomahawk missiles at three Houthi-held coastal radar sites; the Pentagon calls them limited self-defense strikes authorized by President Obama. First US shots against the Houthis in Yemen's war

The Mason fires countermeasures at what officials first said were coastal-defense missiles from Yemen, the third reported incident in about a week; US officials later said the first reports were being reassessed
USS Normandy's boarding team seizes 150 Iranian-made Dehlavieh anti-tank missiles and other arms from a dhow (seized Feb 9, announced Feb 13; logged on the announcement date). Also Iran log #264
US Navy intercepts a fishing vessel carrying 2,116 AK-47s on a route from Iran to Yemen (seized Jan 6, announced Jan 10; logged on the announcement date). Also Iran log #265
A US defense official confirms Houthi forces shot down an MQ-9 Reaper in international airspace off Yemen
Houthis seize the vehicle carrier Galaxy Leader with 25 crew, citing its Israel link; two US defense officials confirm the Houthis seized it
While the Mason responds to the Nov 26 hijacking of the Central Park, at least one ballistic missile from Houthi-held Yemen lands about 10 nautical miles away (01:41 Sanaa time, Nov 27, per CENTCOM)
CENTCOM reports Houthi missiles hit three commercial ships and USS Carney shoots down three drones; CENTCOM says Iran enables the attacks
Houthi missile hits the Maersk Hangzhou; USS Gravely shoots down two more missiles. CENTCOM counts it the 23rd attack on merchant ships in the Red Sea

Helicopters from USS Gravely and USS Eisenhower sink three of four Houthi boats that fired on the Maersk Hangzhou and tried to board; CENTCOM says the crews were killed. Houthis CLAIM ten of their navy members died

Houthis fire 18 drones, 2 anti-ship cruise missiles and 1 anti-ship ballistic missile toward the southern Red Sea; US and UK ships and jets shoot all 21 down. CENTCOM counts it the 26th launch toward Red Sea shipping
USS Laboon, Gravely and Mason, Eisenhower jets and HMS Diamond shoot down all 21 Houthi drones and missiles

First US-UK strikes on Houthi radar, air-defense and missile and drone sites; Biden calls them a defensive action after 27 attacks on shipping. A later PBS report puts it at more than 60 targets at 28 locations
An anti-ship cruise missile is fired from Houthi-held Yemen toward USS Laboon and shot down by a US fighter. First US-acknowledged Houthi targeting after the Jan 12 strikes
CENTCOM says a Houthi missile hits the US-owned and operated Gibraltar Eagle in the southern Red Sea

CENTCOM announces Navy SEALs seized Iranian-made missile parts from a dhow on Jan 11 (logged on the announcement date); two SEALs were lost at sea. First such seizure since Houthi shipping attacks began
A one-way attack drone from Houthi-held Yemen hits the US-owned Genco Picardy
CENTCOM says US forces struck 14 Houthi missiles on launch rails that posed an imminent threat to ships (announced Jan 17; local time may be Jan 18)
Second round of joint US-UK strikes: eight targets including missile launchers, air defenses, radars and buried storage; Tomahawks and Navy jets used
A Houthi missile hits the tanker Marlin Luanda; USS Carney and other coalition ships help
CENTCOM says US and UK forces hit 36 targets at 13 locations: underground storage, command sites, missile systems, drone sites, radars and helicopters
The Rubymar, hit by a Houthi anti-ship ballistic missile on Feb 18, sinks; CENTCOM warns of fertilizer and fuel spill risk
CENTCOM says a Houthi missile hit the bulk carrier True Confidence, the first fatal Houthi strike on shipping
Houthi drone boats hit the Greek-owned Tutor (a photo caption dates the hit to Jun 12); it was reported sunk on Jun 19, the second ship the Houthis have sunk

After repeated Houthi attacks the tanker Sounion, with about 1 million barrels of crude, is on fire; a French destroyer rescues the 29 aboard. The State Department says the Houthis seem set on sinking it
The first of two MQ-9 Reapers the US later confirmed lost to Houthi fire in under a week
The second MQ-9 lost within a week; the Pentagon confirms both on Sep 18 and calls the Houthi claim of 10 Reapers 'not accurate'
Austin says B-2 bombers hit five hardened underground weapons storage sites in Houthi-held Yemen; CENTCOM believes no civilians were killed

CENTCOM says US warplanes hit a missile storage facility and a command-and-control site in Sanaa on Saturday night and early Sunday (Dec 21-22). During the same hours a US cruiser mistakenly shot down a US F/A-18; both pilots survived. Houthis CLAIM they shot it down

Operation Rough Rider opens: US air and naval forces hit dozens of Houthi targets; the Houthi-run health ministry CLAIMS at least 31 killed (another spokesman said 53); first US strikes since the Gaza ceasefire of Jan 19

Houthis CLAIM 18 ballistic and cruise missiles and one drone at the Truman group; a US official said the attack failed; CENTCOM's Grynkewich later said the Houthis missed by over 100 miles; Abdul-Malik al-Houthi says they will target US ships while US strikes continue
A senior defense official says US warships shot down about a dozen Houthi attack drones headed for the Truman group, which was unaffected

US strikes the Ras Isa fuel terminal; CENTCOM says it aimed to cut a fuel source for the Houthis; Houthi-run media CLAIM at least 38 killed and 102 wounded and CENTCOM would not comment on civilian deaths

CENTCOM says Rough Rider has hit 800+ targets and killed hundreds of Houthi fighters and 'numerous Houthi leaders', including senior missile and drone officials, to 'disintegrate' the group; it did not name anyone
Houthi media CLAIM a US strike hit a Saada detention center for African migrants (35 dead, later 68 per the BBC); AFP could not confirm it and CENTCOM was asked for comment
A US official says seven MQ-9 Reapers have gone down since March 15, about $30 million each; he did not say how they were lost
Small boats, then missiles and drones hit the bulk carrier Magic Seas; the crew abandons ship and is rescued; the ship sinks; the Houthis claimed it

Eternity C is attacked for hours and sinks on Jul 9; Reuters reports at least 4 killed and 15 missing early on, with 6 rescued; USNI later counts at least 9 dead, the Houthis' deadliest attack; the Houthis claimed it

CENTCOM announces Yemen's National Resistance Forces seized 750+ tons of Iranian weapons bound for the Houthis (hundreds of missiles, drone engines, radar); the release describes no direct US military role; also relevant to the Iran log's arms-seizure rows (#264, #265)
UKMTO reports an unknown projectile splashing close to the ship on Aug 31; the Houthis announce the attack on Sep 1; the missile missed and all crew are safe
Houthi cruise missile sets the empty cargo ship on fire; crew airlifted off; two crew hurt and one later dies; the Houthis said the owner broke their ban on calling at Israeli ports

Saudi Arabia confirms the Encelia was hit; the Houthis CLAIM missile and drone strikes on it and the tanker Layla; UKMTO reports another tanker hit by an unknown projectile 70 nm southwest of Al Shuqaiq
Also Iran log #98. Houthi attack on Riyadh's King Khalid airport earlier in the week of Oct 10 kills three Saudis including a pilot (date Oct 8 as in the Iran log; NPR says 'earlier that week')
Also Iran log #102. A missile hits the domestic terminals; Saudi civil aviation says 12 killed (incl. one American) and 309 wounded; 291+ flights cancelled
Saudi air defences stop a drone aimed at Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield; the energy ministry does not say who launched it; Reuters and CBS report it among Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
Attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam (Reuters, Oct 21); Al Jazeera lists Dammam airport among recent Houthi targets

Houthis CLAIM missile and drone attacks on Riyadh airport, Dammam, Najran, Khamis Mushait, oil pipelines and Aden; Saudi Arabia says it intercepted missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu; Saudi-led jets bomb Marib, Taiz and other provinces

Saudi-led forces say they intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh and destroyed two launchers in Sanaa; Riyadh airport had reopened two terminals on Oct 25 and the Houthis warned airlines against using it

Trump said on Oct 10 'We may' join; no decision found by Oct 26, and ABC (Oct 20) says the administration is wary of opening a second front.
